title: DO alarms survive a runtime restart: the armed alarm fires in the new process and pre-restart storage is intact
evidence: https://developers.cloudflare.com/durable-objects/api/alarms/ (an alarm is persisted: setAlarm stores it durably and it is delivered even after the object/process restarts; getAlarm reports the armed time)
https://developers.cloudflare.com/durable-objects/api/storage-api/ (storage is durable and outlives the runtime process)
deploy/standalone/e2e.sh (arms an alarm, restarts vrt/vrt-host, asserts the alarm still fires and storage survives on the standalone stack)
examples/standalone-do/main.js (alarm handler + localDisk storage on the standalone stack)
notes: The restart step restarts vrt-host (which supervises workerd) in place via docker compose restart: no volume is recreated and no worker is redeployed, so the only variable is a fresh runtime process. The worker normalizes volatile ids/timestamps into booleans; the alarm chain re-arms itself every 200 ms, so 'fired in the current process' proves the persisted alarm was delivered after the restart.

steps.name: start a self re-arming alarm chain
alarm() fires before the restart in this process
restart the runtime process (vrt-host supervises workerd)
new process: pending alarm fired, storage survived
